days.title: Hei ja tervetuloa!
days.grammar: Personal pronouns (minä, sinä, hän, me, te, he) and the verb olla (to be)
days.task: Introduce yourself in 3 sentences: name, where you live, that you study Finnish.

lessons.title: Tervehdykset & Tutustuminen
lessons.subtitle: Greetings & Basic Introductions
lessons.html:
Greetings & Polite Expressions

In Finnish, formal and informal greetings are widely used depending on the situation:

  • Hei / Moi = Informal "Hi"
  • Päivää / Hyvää päivää = Formal "Good day"
  • Näkemiin = Goodbye (Formal)
  • Moi moi / Hei hei = Bye bye (Informal)

lessons.title: Persoonapronominit & 'Olla'-verbi
lessons.subtitle: Personal Pronouns & Verb 'To Be'
lessons.html:
Conjugating 'Olla' (To Be)

minä olen (I am)
me olemme (we are)
sinä olet (you are)
te olette (you all are)
hän on (he/she is)
he ovat (they are)

quiz.question: How do you say 'Good morning' in Finnish?
quiz.explanation: 'Huomenta' or 'Hyvää huomenta' translates to Good Morning.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Mitä ______?' (How are you?)
quiz.explanation: 'Mitä kuuluu?' literally means 'What is heard?' and translates to 'How are you?'

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Minä ___ opiskelija.'

days.title: Hei ja tervetuloa!
days.theme: Days of the week, alphabet, numbers 0–100
days.grammar: Vowel harmony (a o u vs ä ö y) and long vs short vowels
days.task: Write today's and tomorrow's day, your age, and spell your name in Finnish letters.

lessons.title: Numerot 1-20 & Aika
lessons.subtitle: Numbers 1-20 & Time Basics
lessons.html:
Counting & Asking Time

Numbers 11-19 are formed by adding -toista to numbers 1-9:

11 = yksitoista | 12 = kaksitoista | 15 = viisitoista

lessons.title: Viikonpäivät & Ajankohdat
lessons.subtitle: Days of the Week & Time Expressions
lessons.html:
Days of the Week (+na/nä)

To say "on Monday", add -na / -nä to the day name:

Maanantai -> Maanantaina (On Monday)

quiz.question: What is the Finnish word for number 12?
quiz.explanation: 12 is created by combining Kaksi + toista = Kaksitoista.

quiz.question: How do you say 'On Friday' in Finnish?

days.title: Minkämaalainen sinä olet?
days.grammar: Consonant gradation (k-p-t) in nouns: Helsinki → Helsingissä, Turku → Turussa (see also Minikielioppi p. 311–312)
days.task: Write where you are from, what languages you speak, and where you live now.

lessons.title: KPT-Vaihtelu (Consonant Gradation)
lessons.subtitle: K, P, T Changes in Nouns & Verbs
lessons.html:
Consonant Gradation Basics

Consonants K, P, T weaken when endings close the syllable:

KK -> K (Kukka -> Kukan)

TT -> T (Konsertti -> Konsertin)

T -> D (Katu -> Kadulla)

P -> V (Lapa -> Lavan)

quiz.question: Apply KPT gradation (T -> D): Katu + lla = ______

days.title: Minkämaalainen sinä olet?
days.grammar: Verb type 1 conjugation, negative sentences (en, et, ei…), question words and -ko/-kö
days.task: Write 3 yes/no questions with -ko/-kö and answer each one in the negative.

lessons.title: Vokaaliharmonia & Kysymykset
lessons.subtitle: Vowel Harmony & -Ko/-Kö Questions
lessons.html:
Asking Questions with -ko/-kö

To create a yes/no question, attach -ko or -kö to the verb:

Olet (you are) + ko -> Oletko sinä suomalainen? (Are you Finnish?)

lessons.title: Verbi Tyyppi 1 (Verb Type 1)
lessons.subtitle: Verbs ending in -a / -ä
lessons.html:
Verb Type 1 Rules

Verb Type 1 infinitive ends in a vowel + -a/-ä (puhua, asua, ostaa). Remove the last -a/-ä to get stem, then add endings (-n, -t, vowel doubles, -mme, -tte, -vat).

quiz.question: How do you ask 'Do you speak English?'
Conjugate 'asua' for 'minä': Minä ______
quiz.explanation: Stem of asua is asu- + ending -n = asun.

days.title: Pedro soittaa Mikolle
days.theme: Weather, seasons, months, times of day
days.grammar: Genitive (-n): minun nimeni, Pedron puhelin, Suomen pääkaupunki
days.task: Describe today's weather and name your favourite season and why.

lessons.title: Sää & Vuodenajat
lessons.subtitle: Weather & Seasons
lessons.html:
Describing Weather

Use On + Adjective or [Noun] + verb:

  • On kylmä (It is cold)
  • Sataa vettä (It is raining)

quiz.question: What does 'Aurinko paistaa' mean?

days.title: Pedro soittaa Mikolle
days.theme: Adjectives and personal details (forms, phone calls)
days.grammar: t-plural (talo → talot), consonant gradation in type 1 verbs (nukkua → nukun) (see also Minikielioppi p. 311–312)
days.task: Fill in a pretend registration form in Finnish: nimi, osoite, puhelinnumero, sähköposti.

days.title: Review: chapters 1–3
days.grammar: Review: olla, verb type 1, negatives, genitive, k-p-t gradation
sentences: Tänään on sunnuntai ja sää on kylmä.

days.title: Minä
days.grammar: Partitive singular — after numbers, negatives, mass nouns (see also Minikielioppi p. 313)
sentences: Äitini on pitkä ja hänellä on ruskeat hiukset.
days.task: Describe your family: who they are, how old, what they look like.

lessons.title: Perhe & Ihmissuhteet
lessons.subtitle: Family & Relationships
lessons.html:
Expressing Possession ('Minulla on')

Finnish has no verb for "to have". Instead, use [Person + lla/llä] + on:

Minulla on kissa = I have a cat.
Sinulla on koira = You have a dog.

lessons.title: Terveys & Keho
lessons.subtitle: Health & Human Body
lessons.html:
Expressing Aches ('[Body part] särkee')

To say something hurts:

Päätä särkee = Head hurts.
Vatsaa särkee = Stomach hurts.

quiz.question: How do you say 'I have a family'?
How do you say 'I am sick today'?

days.title: Minä
days.grammar: Minulla on… (having) and partitive verbs (rakastaa, odottaa, auttaa)
days.task: Write a short shop dialogue: you look for an item, ask the price and the size.

lessons.title: Ulkoasu & Vaatteet
lessons.subtitle: Appearance & Clothing
lessons.html:
Plural Nouns Intro

Basic nominative plural adds -t to the end:

Kenkä -> Kengät | Takki -> Takit

quiz.question: What is the plural form of 'Kenkä' (shoe)?

days.title: Meidän tavallinen päivä
days.theme: Daily routine and telling the time
days.grammar: All verb types 1–5 in the present tense
days.task: Write your normal weekday from morning to evening with times.

lessons.title: Verbi Tyyppi 2 (Verb Type 2)
lessons.subtitle: Verbs ending in -da / -dä
lessons.html:
Verb Type 2 Stem Creation

Drop -da / -dä to find the stem:

Syödä -> syö- + n = syön (I eat)

quiz.question: Conjugate 'juoda' for 'sinä': Sinä ______

days.title: Meidän tavallinen päivä
days.grammar: verb + verb (haluan syödä) and verb + partitive (juon kahvia)
days.task: Write a message suggesting a meeting: day, time and place.

lessons.title: Vapaa-aika & Harrastukset
lessons.subtitle: Free Time & Hobbies
lessons.html:
Expressing Likes ('Pitää')

Use Minä pidän + [Noun + -sta/-stä]:

Pidän musiikista = I like music.

quiz.question: How do you say 'I like music'?

days.title: Pedro ja Hanna etsivät asuntoa
days.grammar: Place cases: -ssa/-ssä, -sta/-stä, -Vn (inside cases) and -lla/-lta/-lle (outside cases) (see also Minikielioppi p. 314–315)
sentences: Keittiössä on pöytä ja neljä tuolia.
days.task: Describe your home: type of building, rooms, and what is in each room.

lessons.title: Koti & Asuminen
lessons.subtitle: Home & Furniture
lessons.html:
Inessiivi (-ssa/-ssä)

Means "inside something":

Talo -> Talossa (In the house)
Huone -> Huoneessa (In the room)

quiz.question: Add inessiivi ending (-ssa) to 'talo': talo -> ______

days.title: Muutto
days.theme: Moving house and calling the landlord
days.grammar: Huoneessa on… (there is), tämä/tuo/se, imperative (sinä): tule! istu!
days.task: Write a call to a landlord (huoltoyhtiö): something is broken, ask them to fix it.

days.title: Review: chapters 4–6
days.grammar: Review: partitive, all verb types, place cases, imperative
days.task: Run the review quiz for days 8–13, then write 10 sentences: family, day, home.

days.title: Kylässä
days.grammar: Word types ending in -e, -nen and -i (huone → huoneessa, nainen → naisen, kieli → kielen)
days.task: Describe how you get from home to the city centre and what is there.

lessons.title: Kaupunki & Liikenne
lessons.subtitle: City & Transportation
lessons.html:
Means of Transport (-lla/-llä)

Use the adessive ending to mean "by [vehicle]":

Bussi -> bussilla (by bus)
Juna -> junalla (by train)

quiz.question: How do you say 'by train' in Finnish?
quiz.explanation: Adding -lla gives the meaning 'by means of train'.

days.title: Kylässä
days.theme: Visiting friends and at the hotel
days.grammar: Imperfect (past tense) of olla, tulla, mennä + minulla oli
days.task: Write about yesterday: where you were, where you went, when you came home.

lessons.title: Menneisyys & Imperfekti
lessons.subtitle: Past Tense Basics
lessons.html:
Simple Past Tense marker '-i-'

Past tense is formed by adding -i- before personal ending:

Puhu- + i + n -> Puhuin (I spoke)

quiz.question: What is the past tense form of 'Olen' (I am)?

days.title: Onnea uuteen kotiin!
days.grammar: Partitive with food and materials (kahvia, leipää, maitoa)
days.task: Write a shopping list and a short party invitation in Finnish.

lessons.title: Kahvilassa & Ruoka
lessons.subtitle: At the Cafe & Ordering Food
lessons.html:
Ordering Expressions

Polite ways to order food/drink in Finnish:

  • Otan... = I will take...
  • Saisinko... = Could I have...
  • ..., kiitos. = ..., please.

lessons.title: Ainekset & Kaupassa Käynti
lessons.subtitle: Grocery Shopping & Partitive Intro
lessons.html:
Partitiivi (Partitive Case) Intro

Used after numbers > 1, uncounted substances, or ongoing actions:

Maito -> Maitoa | Leipä -> Leipää

quiz.question: What does 'Paljonko maksaa?' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Paljonko maksaa?' asks for the total cost or price.

quiz.question: Which case is used after numbers higher than 1?
quiz.explanation: Numbers > 1 require the noun in Partitive singular (e.g., kaksi omenaa).

days.title: Onnea uuteen kotiin!

days.task: Write your birthday and 3 holidays as dates, then give directions to a place near you.

lessons.title: Suomalainen Kulttuuri
lessons.subtitle: Finnish Culture & Expressions
lessons.html:
Key Cultural Words

Understanding culture enhances language fluency! Sisu, Sauna, and Kahvitauko are cornerstones of Finnish life.

quiz.question: What does the famous Finnish concept 'Sisu' refer to?
quiz.explanation: Sisu represents mental fortitude and determination.
